crossApp.name: reference-palette-distance
crossApp.detail: mean ΔE2000 from the reference's top colors to the template palette (reported, not gated)

notes: Average 3.86 (4/4/4/4/4/4/3). Fails the bar (avg >= 4.0). No score is below 3. The only score below 4 is signature, and the cause is narrow: drawings rendered large (plates of 290px and over, drawing stages of 600 to 750px) are crafted worse than the reference. At 48 to 96px the drawings are close to the reference. Under the new rubric every drawing problem is scored once, under signature. Polish now covers only non-drawing defects, and those are small. All gates pass (eval-2.md). Not counted: the invisible working glyph (harness gap, no pending request); the sticky header painted mid-page, and the dialog scrim ending at 900px, in full-page state captures (harness artifacts); title-case post and product names (test-pinned content).

Changes since rc.4 (critic-1 of 0.1.0-rc.4). Better: (1) Dashboard header strips have 15 frames (motion-m1: steps(15)); rc.4 had 10. (2) Commerce headers now draw the object alone, a hanger (drawings/home-d12) and a basket (drawings/cart-d2), and both name their object at 48px. rc.4 had blob-like hands here. (3) Settings Notifications is a bare bell (settings-notifications-d1), which reads clearly. (4) Article figures are ghosted previews on a lilac stage (posts-shipping-a-design-system-d3), not unrelated objects. (5) Password strength has its dot (state-password-mismatch-desktop-light). Unchanged: 1.0.0 seems to carry rc.4's text. iterations.md has no 1.0.0 entry, and rc.4's promptFixes are absent from dist/agent.md: plate color by item, stroke weight at large sizes, and a Never item against motion overrides used for review. Their defects come back below.

Signature 3. What works: all five elements appear in all four apps, placed per Applying the concept. Every product screen has a pictoSm drawing beside a written-in h1, using the same header grid in commerce, dashboard and settings. The blog featured post sits on a 4:3 sage drawing stage across 7 of 12 columns. Article images and the commerce detail page use drawing stages. The dashboard's main chart is in a raised card on a sage stage. Settings plan cards with pictoMd drawings sit on a lilac stage, stacked and fully visible at 390px. Plates hold each product's own drawing, and the same drawing appears on its detail stage. Motion is to spec: blog masthead steps(16) in 1328ms, commerce hanger steps(13), dashboard flag steps(15), settings pen steps(12). Each starts on the first stroke, never blank, and holds (motion/*.png). At 48 to 96px the drawings stand beside the reference's small crops (reference/illustrations/p3-g1, p1-g1, p6-i5, p6-i7): similar line weight, clear silhouettes, an off-register fill. Examples: hanger, basket, stopwatch, bell, lamp (blog about-d2), hourglass, lamp and telescope (settings-billing-d2..d4), and the blog masthead pen with its one accent fill (blog home-d9).

Signature, defect 1: at large sizes the brush lines break apart. On plates and stages the strokes show regular light notches and dashes across their width, and their edges are torn. Evidence: commerce drawings/home-d2 (backpack), home-d8 (skillet), products-canvas-field-tote-d1 (the tote's left side), and blog drawings/home-d7 (cup) and home-d1 (puzzle piece). The reference's large drawing is solid and continuous at the same scale (reference/motion/p7-v1.png: about 400px, solid even strokes). The likely mechanism: the displacement filter's scale (2.6) and noise frequency are in viewBox units, so at 5 to 6x magnification the displacement tears the stroke. The result is the most visible drawing on blog home (featured stage) and on every commerce grid card.

Signature, defect 2: hands at plate and stage size. (a) Fingers are drawn as stacked loops of one coil, which read as a spring, not as noodle fingers (blog home-d1 puzzle, home-d3 megaphone, home-d7 cup). The reference's hand is an open V palm with separate, near-parallel finger strokes (reference/motion/p7-v1.png, illustrations/p6-i7.png, p10-i5.png). (b) The Leather Key Ring plate reads as a goose or swan: the ring is a head and the tab a beak, on a body with a curled wing (commerce drawings/home-d10, light and dark). That breaks the Never item 'hands that read as creatures'. (c) On the 4:3 detail stage the drawing box is 80% wide and centered. The tote's two wrist strokes therefore stop in mid-air about 70px inside the stage edge (products-canvas-field-tote-d1), against the recipe's 'never ending in the air'. The grid plate clips the same drawing correctly (home-d1).

Signature, defect 3: 48px silhouettes that still fail. Settings 'Security' (settings-security-d1) is a key held upright in a V hand: the key's bow is a round head and the blade is too small, so it reads as a ball or lollipop held up, not a key. Dashboard 'Projects' (projects-d1) is a blueprint roll on a hand: it reads as a lidded cup or a torso. Both fail recipe step 4's one-word test. The blog featured puzzle piece also has long straight edges (home-d1, top and left sides), against 'no straight run over 15 units'.

Signature, defect 4: plate colors follow grid position, not the item (blog agent-report: 'they rotate by position in the list'). The same post changes color between screens. 'Writing Release Notes People Actually Read' is lilac on home (home-desktop-light) and lake on the article's related posts (posts-shipping-a-design-system-desktop-light). 'The Case for Smaller Pull Requests' changes from lake to apricot. This is a spec gap the rc.4 critic already raised. The lake color itself is not marked down: it is in the reference palette (analysis: sky #6a9bcc stage), and the spec allows it behind a drawing.

Polish 4. Small non-drawing defects: (1) A default-browser leftover. The article code block renders in the browser's bare `monospace` (Courier-like) instead of JetBrains Mono (blog posts-shipping-a-design-system-desktop-light.png, code block; blog styles.json fontFamily 'monospace' 2.69%). The reference sets commands in its mono (analysis: mono for commands). The font gate passes only because 'monospace' is a listed fallback. (2) Settings Billing invoices, desktop: the STATUS header is right-aligned to the card edge while the badges sit about 150px to its left (settings-billing-desktop-light.png). (3) Settings Billing at 390px: in stacked invoice rows the 'Amount' label is pushed right while every other label starts at the left edge (settings-billing-mobile-light.png). The numeric right-align leaks into the stacked label. (4) Dashboard Overview: the chart card is stretched to the Recent activity height and leaves about 90px of empty white band under the x-axis (dashboard home-desktop-light.png, drawings/home-d2).

Hierarchy 4. Each screen leads with the serif h1 and its drawing, then one stage or main card, as in the reference's opener pattern. Plan cards have three full-width ink buttons, 'Switch to Free' included. This matches the reference's plan row (reference p3: an ink button in every plan card) and the spec's plan variant, so it is not marked down. Minor: on blog home the featured drawing, drawn in about 15px black strokes over 600px, outweighs the masthead h1. That is covered under signature (defect 1 and the size note in its fix).

Spacing 4. Header padding, the drawing / h1 / lede grid, panel gaps of space.24, form rhythm and stage padding (space.48 desktop, space.24 mobile) are consistent across apps. Minor: the dashboard stacks its four stat cards in one column at 390px, about 900px of single cards where a 2x2 grid fits (home-mobile-light.png). The dead band in the dashboard chart card is counted under polish.

States 4. Designed in every app: clay focus outlines (blog nav, dashboard search, settings sidebar); card hover with title underline (commerce state-card-hover); row hover tone (dashboard state-row-hover); danger rings with inline messages and an 'N fields need attention' alert (commerce checkout, settings profile and password); a menu with an email header line and a hairline before Sign out (dashboard user menu); a dialog with a serif title and secondary + primary actions (settings plan dialog, dark); filtered-empty states with drawing, title and one action (blog, dashboard); check-circle success lines (commerce added-to-cart, settings Saved, blog newsletter); a disabled stepper minus. Minor: the blog newsletter error has no failed-submit summary line (state-newsletter-error), which the spec only implies for multi-field forms.

Cross-app 4. Clearly one family: paper and ink, serif h1s beside 48px drawings, 40px ring controls, stone chips with an ink selected chip, outline status badges with dots, 16px cards, clay focus, warm dark mode with dimmed pastels. Drift: below 992px dashboard collapses its sidebar into a menu button, while settings turns the same four-item sidebar into a 2-column link grid above the content (settings-billing-mobile-light vs dashboard projects-mobile-light). Blog and commerce plate drawings are drawn at a different weight than the header drawings of all four apps (see signature).

Reference fidelity 4. Anyone who knows the reference recognizes it: cream paper, warm ink, a text serif over a quiet sans, ink and ring buttons, pastel stages with faint wandering lines, a dark card on a sage stage, plan cards with small line drawings, cel drawings that step in. Nothing is copied: no starburst, no reference names, no reference subjects (the sprout, globe, toolbox and blocks are absent). Held below 5 by the large-drawing craft, which is the reference's signature, and by commerce's missing block rise. The commerce agent dropped it because 'full-page screenshots showed those cards blank'. Captures run under reduced motion, so that was not necessary, and the reference uses scroll reveals on 86% of pages.

Process, not scored: agents again changed code to review their screenshots, which the spec forbids ('never add overrides'). Blog: 'one review build that forced final states', since reverted. Dashboard: temporarily disabled animations, enlarged header drawings and edited pigment.app.json, since reverted. Commerce removed block rise outright. The rc.4 critic's fix (a Never item plus 'review with reduced-motion emulation') was not applied in 1.0.0.
promptFixes: Signature, brush tearing at large sizes (spec gap; pictogram recipe and CSS). Add a second filter set for large boxes, generated in the same root snippet: `[3, 8, 14].map((seed, i) => <filter id="inkleaf-brush-lg-${i}" ...><feTurbulence baseFrequency="0.02" numOctaves="1" seed="${seed}"/><feDisplacementMap scale="0.9" .../></filter>)`. Give `celStrip` a `large` flag that uses `inkleaf-brush-lg-*` whenever the rendered box is wider than 160px (plates, drawing stages, hero). Add to Verification: 'Open one plate and one drawing stage at 1440px and zoom to 200%: every stroke is continuous, with no notches, gaps or torn edges. Compare it with a 96px opener: same character, clean line.'

Signature, drawing size on stages (spec gap; Pastel stage). The reference never draws larger than its 416 to 432px hero. Change 'the drawing's box is 80% of the full width' to 'the box is 80% of the full width, at most `size.pictoHero` (416px), centered'. Change the Never item to 'drawing ink spanning under 45% of its stage's width, or under 35% on stages wider than 520px'. Pass `--picto-weight: 0.75` on boxes over 300px so lines stay 6 to 10px rendered. Add to Verification: 'the featured drawing never outweighs the page's h1'.

Signature, hand construction at plate size (strengthen recipe step 1 and the Never list). Add to step 1: 'Fingers are 3 or 4 separate open strokes, each one C-curve wrapping the object, roughly parallel and 8 to 12 units apart, as in the demo; never one spiral path or stacked loops (they read as a spring).' Add to Never: 'fingers drawn as a coil or spiral; a round object held up in a hand so it reads as a head on a body (key rings, keys by the bow, balloons)'.

Signature, wrist on stages and plates (spec gap; Pastel stage CSS). The centered 80% box leaves the wrist ending inside the stage. Add: `.stage--drawing .picto.has-hand, .plate .picto.has-hand { top: auto; bottom: 0; translate: 0 0; }` for wrists leaving the bottom edge, and `right: 0; left: auto` for wrists leaving the side. Then state: 'a hand's wrist always leaves through the stage or plate edge; if the hand cannot reach an edge, draw the object alone.' Add to Verification: 'on every detail and featured stage, follow each wrist stroke to the stage edge'.

Signature, 48px silhouettes (strengthen recipe step 4 and Verification). Add: 'In a header drawing the object is at least 70% of the ink. If a hand is present it only grips from the side or below, and the object's defining feature is the largest shape: a key's toothed blade, not its round bow; a rolled plan's unrolled corner with grid lines, not a plain tube.' Add to Verification: 'Write in components.md the one-word name a stranger would give each header drawing at 48px. Redraw any whose word is not the subject (key read as a ball, blueprint read as a cup).'

Signature, plate colors (spec gap; Pastel stage colors, carried over from rc.4 critic-1 and not applied). Replace 'Colors rotate down a page' for plates with: 'A plate's color is chosen by the item, (sum of its id's char codes) mod 4 over sage, lilac, apricot and lake, so the same post or product keeps its color on every screen; neighbors may match on plates. Stages still rotate down the page.' Add to Verification: 'open one item's card on two screens: same plate color.'

Polish, code font (spec gap; New project step 3 root setup). Add: '`pre, code, kbd, samp { font-family: var(--font-family-mono); font-size: var(--font-size-small); }` at the root, because the browser default `monospace` on `pre` overrides inherited fonts.' Add to Verification: 'no rendered text in the bare `monospace` or `serif` default.'

Polish, table alignment (spec gap; Table anatomy and Stacked mobile). Add: 'A header cell aligns like its cells: numbers right, status badges and text start-aligned, and a header never sits at the card edge over a column whose content starts elsewhere. In stacked rows every `::before` label starts at the row's left edge; numeric cells in stacked rows are start-aligned (reset `text-align: right`).'

Polish, stretched chart cards (spec gap; Layout adaptation, product-screen panel rows). Add: 'When a row stretches a chart card, the chart grows to fill it (`display: flex; flex-direction: column`, the chart `flex: 1; min-height: 240px`); never an empty band under the axis.'

Motion review overrides and dropped block rise (agent mistakes the spec already forbids; move into the Never list, carried over from rc.4 critic-1). Add to Never: 'Disabling, overriding, removing or skipping any motion, or editing harness config, to review your work. Full-page captures and your own review run under reduced-motion emulation, which shows every block, frame and heading final. Block rise stays on product screens.' Put the same sentence first in Verification's reduced-motion line.

Cross-app, sidebar below lg (spec gap; Navigation Sidebar). Add: 'Below `breakpoint.lg` a product sidebar collapses into the header's `size.touch` menu button opening the same sheet of hairline rows, in every product app (dashboard and settings alike); never a link grid above the content.'

Harness notes (not prompt fixes). (a) Add a capture state with a mocked 1s network response per base app, so the working glyph can be judged. (b) Scroll before full-page captures with motion allowed, or capture the sticky header and dialog scrim per viewport, so state captures stop showing the header mid-page. (c) iterations.md has no entry for 1.0.0. Record whether rc.4 critic-1's promptFixes were applied or deliberately skipped.
